evidenceBasis: Direct visual inspection of originalSourcePNG only; input-freeze read first. No candidate, history, author findings, or supporting comparison read before this inventory.

apparatus: Unbathed corrugated bellows resting on a bottom base within an upright frame.
Horizontal frame crosspiece above the bellows, central vertical adjustment rod with knob, and movable bellows top plate below the crosspiece.
Graduated vertical strip on the left side of the frame.
Curved hose connects the right side of the bellows/top-plate assembly to the left fitting of a separate round pressure gauge.
Pressure gauge has peripheral tick marks, indistinct microglyphs, a central needle and counterweight, upright support, horizontal fittings and spread-foot base.
Long gauge pointer points upper right; the short opposite portion points lower left.
A separate slanted thermometer-like graduated instrument lies below the hose, outside the bellows and without a bath.
subparts.qualitativeState: Initial, relatively shorter bellows than the upper-right expanded state; no numeric volume, pressure or temperature read from source.

apparatus: Same bellows/frame/central rod/top-plate apparatus, visibly expanded relative to the upper-left subpart.
Rod and knob project high above the apparatus.
Bellows assembly is surrounded by an open cylindrical bath with elliptical rim and visible curved walls, sitting on a rectangular supporting block.
Slanted thermometer stands along the bath's left side with its lower end inside the bath, left of the bellows rather than inside the bellows gas volume.
Hose exits the right upper apparatus, arches above the rim and descends to the separate pressure gauge's left fitting.
Round gauge with support and spread-foot base repeats the first gauge's long-pointer upper-right direction.
subparts.qualitativeState: Bellows expansion relative to first subpart; qualitatively same pressure-pointer direction as first; bath arrangement supplies thermal context, not a readable numeric bath temperature.

apparatus: Bellows/frame/rod/top-plate assembly compressed relative to the upper-right expanded subpart.
Central knob/rod remains above the bath; top plate is lower relative to the expanded state.
Cylindrical bath remains around the bellows on a rectangular supporting block.
Thermometer again stands at the left of the bath with its lower end within the bath, outside the bellows.
Hose again connects the right upper apparatus to the separate gauge's left fitting.
Gauge has the same essential round dial, central needle, support and spread-foot base, but its long needle points lower right; the short opposite portion points upper left.
subparts.qualitativeState: Compression relative to second subpart, changed pressure indication, continuing bath arrangement. No required volume ordering between first and third subparts and no numeric needle reading inferred.

relationshipsToPreserve: All three real source subparts must remain, with their apparatus assemblies and separate connected gauges.
Bellows lie inside their frames; central rods act on bellows top plates, not on the gauges or thermometers.
Each hose connects its bellows apparatus to its own pressure gauge.
Second bellows is expanded relative to first; third is compressed relative to second.
First and second long gauge pointers point upper right; third points lower right.
Only second and third subparts have surrounding baths and supporting blocks.
Second and third thermometers are placed in bath at the left of the bellows, not in the bellows gas space.
First thermometer-like instrument is separate and slanted below the hose.
